title: Papier Blanc Journal
subtitle: This blog focuses on using Open Source technology to achieve more, or using 'dumb' tech to solve modern problems.

posts.title: Building Sovereign Infrastructure with Proxmox and Self-Hosted Platforms
posts.excerpt: Why organizations with sensitive data increasingly choose on-prem virtualization, open source building blocks, and internal-by-default operations.
posts.author: Papier Blanc

sections.title: Why Sovereignty Matters
body: For many organizations, infrastructure is no longer just a hosting decision. It is a control decision. Where systems run, who can access them, and how data moves between environments directly affect privacy, risk, and operational resilience.

A self-hosted datacenter model gives teams more control over the critical path. Instead of routing core systems through external platforms by default, companies can keep sensitive workloads, private research, and internal knowledge inside infrastructure they actually govern.

sections.title: What a Strong On-Prem Foundation Usually Includes
items: Clustered virtualization for flexible workload placement and recovery
Internal identity, monitoring, backup, and automation services
Network segmentation between labs, production, and private workloads
Operational visibility into how systems are configured and changed

sections.title: Example Infrastructure Definition
sections.code:
cluster:
  platform: proxmox
  nodes:
    - name: pve-01
      role: compute
    - name: pve-02
      role: compute
    - name: pve-03
      role: backup
services:
  - identity
  - monitoring
  - internal-registry
  - backup-orchestrator
policy:
  internet_access: restricted
  data_location: on_prem

sections.title: Operational Direction
body: Open source is valuable here not just because of cost, but because it gives the organization direct visibility and architectural control.
That matters most when the environment handles private company information or research that should not casually leave the network perimeter.

posts.title: Why Custom In-House Software Still Wins for Exact Business Requirements
posts.excerpt: Generic software often fails where business details matter most. Custom systems let companies design around real workflows instead of vendor assumptions.
posts.author: Papier Blanc

sections.title: The Hidden Cost of Generic Tools
body: Off-the-shelf platforms can look efficient at first, but they frequently create friction where the business is most specific: approvals, exceptions, internal terminology, and cross-team handoffs.
That friction usually shows up as manual workarounds, duplicate entry, brittle integrations, and increasing process debt.

sections.quote: The best internal software often feels obvious in hindsight because it matches the company so closely that people stop noticing the system and focus on the work.

sections.title: A Better Internal Platform Usually Improves
items: Workflow precision for approvals and special-case handling
Operational clarity through company-specific language and models
Long-term adaptability as the organization evolves

sections.title: Service Boundary Sketch

posts.title: Leaner Engineering Organizations in the Age of AI
posts.excerpt: AI does not just change productivity. It changes how engineering teams should be structured, where management adds value, and when restructuring becomes necessary.
posts.author: Papier Blanc

sections.title: Restructuring Is a Strategic Choice
body: As engineering teams gain leverage from AI-assisted workflows, the organization has to reconsider old assumptions about team size, management layers, and coordination structures.
The question is not whether every role disappears. The question is whether each role still creates enough value relative to the new execution model.

sections.title: Signals That an Engineering Org Needs Redesign
items: Too many people coordinating work and too few shipping it
Managers acting as process routers instead of leaders
Technical decisions escalated through several non-technical layers
High meeting load with low decision clarity

sections.title: A Practical View
body: Modern structures often favor smaller, more senior teams with clearer ownership and fewer translation layers between business intent and technical execution.
That does not mean removing leadership. It means distinguishing leadership from overhead.
